extracted.intended_audience: federal judges, litigators, and law clerks handling equitable injunctions/unfair-competition cases between news services
extracted.subtask_description: A defendant's legal brief opposing a temporary injunction in an unfair-competition / news-service dispute, setting out factual rebuttal and legal standards (clean-hands, standing, evidence sufficiency, industry custom) relevant to injunctive relief. Mostly directed at persuading a court not to grant preliminary equitable relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clean hands / equitable bar
rubrics_metrics.description: 'He who comes into equity must come with clean hands' — a plaintiff engaged in similar inequitable practices will be denied equitable relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If complainant itself has engaged in like misconduct (e.g., receiving or using confidential information of defendant), the court should refuse injunctive relief. The brief cites the equitable maxims and argues the court should not lend its aid to one guilty of inequity.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Practice' vs. isolated misconduct standard for injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: To justify a temporary injunction against alleged systematic misconduct (e.g., seducing employees), plaintiff must show a practice or course of conduct, not merely a single isolated act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One isolated wrongful act by a low-level employee, unacknowledged by defendant officers and not shown to be part of a regular practice, is insufficient to brand defendant a 'business pirate' or to justify a temporary injunction; courts require evidence of likely continuation or systematic behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing in equity when mutual wrongdoing exists
rubrics_metrics.description: A plaintiff lacks standing in equity to complain where it has committed similar wrongs against the defendant (reciprocal misconduct undermines equitable standing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defendant may assert that complainant cannot complain about disclosures where complainant knowingly received defendant's confidential information; such reciprocal conduct defeats equitable claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge/intent element for liability
rubrics_metrics.description: Liability (or equitable relief) requires proof that defendant knew of the source's exclusivity/obligation (i.e., knowledge that information was confidential or subject to an exclusive arrangement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there is nothing in the moving papers showing defendant knew a particular employee was obligated to furnish news exclusively to complainant, that missing knowledge is an essential element the plaintiff must prove.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence sufficiency and clarity for temporary injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: A temporary injunction should be granted only on sufficiently clear, convincing, and unequivocal evidence establishing the wrong and the likelihood of its continuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brief argues the proofs fail to establish the alleged misconduct clearly enough to warrant preliminary injunction; courts should demand concrete, corroborated proof rather than insinuation or inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness/protest and acquiescence (failure to object)
rubrics_metrics.description: A plaintiff's failure to protest or notify the defendant of alleged wrongful acts, despite knowledge for a considerable time, weakens its claim for equitable relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay or failure to protest may indicate acquiescence or reduce the urgency/seriousness of the claimed injury and is relevant to whether a court should grant injunctive relief (arguments touching on laches/acquiescence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry custom as a defense to unfairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Longstanding custom among news-gathering agencies (e.g., copying from early bulletins/early editions) can render certain practices lawful and protect defendants from equitable relief claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the contested conduct is a recognized custom 'from time immemorial' among news distributors (including the plaintiff), that custom may negate the claim of unfairness and justify denial of injunctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of specificity and corroboration in affidavits
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits supporting a motion for injunction must contain particularized facts and, where critical, corroborating witness statements; vague, self-serving, or uncorroborated affidavits are weak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brief points out missing affidavits from relevant superiors and emphasizes that witnesses who allege 'tips' must provide particulars; absence of key corroboration undermines the motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to prove inducement or breach by members
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations that defendant induced members to violate their by-laws or agreements must be supported by evidence; mere insinuation or general accusation is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To enjoin inducement-of-breach conduct, plaintiff must present evidence that specific members were induced and that contractual/by-law obligations were known and breached; broad allegations without proof should not justify relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of injunctive relief must be supported by proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for broad prohibitory injunctions (e.g., forbidding 'any other unfair or corrupt methods') require particularized proof of the specific unfair methods alleged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts should not issue sweeping injunctions absent evidence of particular unfair practices; injunctions must be tailored to the misconduct demonstrated by the record.
